ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows, from left to right, a paper strip undergoing three folds. On the far left is a slanted paper strip, with a dashed fold crease on the strip, drawn as an approximately horizontal line, and α is marked between this dashed fold crease and the edge of the paper strip. The following figures are connected in sequence by arrows, showing the overlapping strip-shaped parts formed after the paper strip is folded along the crease. In the last figure, the paper strip forms three directions similar to a sector, and the bottom central included angle is marked β. Reasoning: Looking at the figure from left to right, the crease of the first fold is the horizontal dashed line in the far-left figure, and α is the angle between the crease and the edge of the paper strip. Folding is equivalent to mirror reflection about the crease, so after the first fold, the directions of the two overlapping paper strips are symmetric about this crease. The acute angle formed between them is 180°−2α. Substituting α=70°, we get 180°−2×70°=40°. The next two folds are also reflections, and reflection preserves angles, so this 40° angle will be transferred successively into three copies in the final sector-like structure. The β in the final figure is composed of three identical 40° angles, therefore β=3×40°=120°.

raw_record.question_text: A strip of paper is folded three times as shown. Determine $\beta$ if $\alpha=70^{\circ}$.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram left to right: the first crease is the dotted horizontal segment across the slanted strip, and α is the angle between that crease and the strip edge. After this first fold, the two strip directions are mirror images across the horizontal crease, so the acute angle formed between the two overlapped strip directions is 180°−2α. With α=70°, this gives 40°. Then follow the next two drawn folds: each new fold transfers one more copy of this same 40° angle into the final fan-shaped arrangement because folding is a reflection and preserves the angle between the strip edge and the crease. In the last picture, β is made from three congruent 40° angle pieces around the central folded point. Therefore β=3×40°=120°.
